title: isitahack incident tables
description: Column definitions for the CSV files in an incident folder. The field vocabulary (name, type, constraints, foreignKeys) follows Frictionless Table Schema. Every 'description' is written for the agent filling the column in: it says what the column is for.

claims.description: Every labelled claim on the page, one row each. Theories, timeline facts, findings and side threads are all claims; 'group' says which set a claim belongs to.

fields.name: claim_id
fields.description: Permanent id for this claim, c plus a number (c001). Never reused or renumbered.

fields.name: group
fields.description: The set this claim belongs to, for example theory, timeline, side-thread, ruled-out. A 'claims' section in incident.json shows one group.

fields.name: claim_text
fields.description: The claim in one short line, as a reader would recognise it (for example 'Cyberattack' or 'National ground stop ordered'). This is the row's heading.

fields.name: summary
fields.description: One or two plain sentences saying what the sources say, attributed to who said it. Shown while the row is closed, so it must stand alone.

fields.name: detail
fields.description: Everything else worth knowing: caveats, conflicting accounts, quotes. Shown when the row is opened. Inline Markdown only (links, bold, code).

fields.name: label
fields.description: How well supported the claim is. Exactly one of the six labels, in full words.

fields.name: source_ids
fields.description: The sources that support this claim, primary source first, separated by semicolons. Every claim has at least one.

fields.name: why_it_supports
fields.description: One line: what the primary source shows and why that backs the claim.

fields.name: notes
fields.description: Working notes for the desk. Not shown on the page.

fields.name: last_checked
fields.description: When an agent last re-checked this claim against its sources. Leave empty only for a claim carried over from before this was recorded; fill it in at the next re-check.

sources.description: Every source cited anywhere in the incident, one row each. Claims, quotes, charts, images and tables point here by source_id.

fields.name: source_id
fields.description: Permanent id for this source, s plus a number (s001).

fields.name: source_url
fields.description: Public http(s) address of the source. Nothing behind a login.

fields.name: source_name
fields.description: Publisher or document name as a reader should see it, for example 'FAA ATCSCC Advisory 005'. Never a reporter's name.

fields.name: source_tier
fields.description: 1 official or primary statement, 2 independent reputable outlet, 3 named researcher or technical analysis, 4 social post from an official account or named expert, 5 rumor.

fields.name: independence_group
fields.description: A short name for where the reporting originated. Outlets repeating one report share a value and count as one source. Leave empty for Tier 1.

fields.name: source_date
fields.description: When the source was published. A date, or a date and time with offset if the time is known. Leave empty if the source does not say; never guess.

fields.name: retrieved_at
fields.description: When an agent last read the source. Required when link_status is ok or archived; leave empty when the source could not be read.

fields.name: archive_url
fields.description: Public archived copy. Required when link_status is dead.

fields.name: link_status
fields.description: ok, dead, blocked (the site blocks automated access or needs a login, so it was not re-read) or archived.

fields.name: last_checked
fields.description: When the link was last checked.

timeline.description: Dated events in the order they happened. Each event takes its label and source from one claim, so the label lives in one place.

fields.name: event_id
fields.description: Permanent id for this event, t plus a number (t001).

fields.name: event_time
fields.description: When the event happened: a date and time with timezone offset, or a date alone when the source gives only the day. Rows are shown in file order, so keep them in the order things happened.

fields.name: event_end_time
fields.description: When it ended, if the event is a span (for example a radar outage from 12:19 to 12:44).

fields.name: time_text
fields.description: Only when the time cannot be written as a clock time: how it should read on the page, for example 'Before 3:54 PM' or 'night'. It replaces the clock time; the date still comes from event_time.

fields.name: time_basis
fields.description: stated if the source gives the time, approximate if it gives a rough time, inferred if the desk worked it out. For inferred, say how in notes.

fields.name: event_text
fields.description: What happened, in one attributed line.

fields.name: claim_id
fields.description: The claim that carries this event's label, evidence and source.

fields.name: notes
fields.description: The anchor for an inferred time, or other working notes.

questions.description: The questions people are asking and the rumors going round, each with a plain answer once there is one. The page's headline question is the row named by main_question_id in incident.json.

fields.name: question_id
fields.description: Permanent id, q plus a number (q001).

fields.name: kind
fields.description: question for something people are asking, rumor for a claim going round.

fields.name: question_text
fields.description: The question in the words a reader would use. The main question becomes the page title, so it must name its subject and stay within 70 characters: 'Was the FAA ground stop a cyberattack?', never 'Was it a hack?'.

fields.name: state
fields.description: open while the desk is still working on it, answered once answer_text and label are filled in.

fields.name: answer_text
fields.description: The plain answer, one or two calm sentences. Lead with the answer, not the threat.

fields.name: label
fields.description: The label on the answer. Required once answered. Use Not established when the evidence settles nothing.

fields.name: claim_ids
fields.description: The claims the answer rests on, separated by semicolons. Required once answered.

fields.name: rumor_type
fields.description: For rumors: what kind it turned out to be.

fields.name: what_would_settle_it
fields.description: What evidence would answer this. Required while open, and when the label is Not established.

fields.name: opened_at
fields.description: When the desk first recorded the question.

fields.name: answered_at
fields.description: When the current answer was written.

quotes.description: Statements quoted word for word, with who said them. Use for official statements and for transcribed audio.

fields.name: quote_id
fields.description: Permanent id, v plus a number (v001).

fields.name: group
fields.description: The set this quote belongs to, for example official-statement or radio. A 'quotes' section shows one group.

fields.name: quote_text
fields.description: The exact words. Never paraphrased, never invented.

fields.name: speaker
fields.description: The organisation, or a public official by name and role. Never a private person, a reporter or a handle.

fields.name: context
fields.description: Where or how it was said, for example 'White House briefing'.

fields.name: said_at
fields.description: When it was said, if known. A date, or a date and time with offset.

fields.name: source_id
fields.description: The source the quote was taken from.

fields.name: confidence
fields.description: For transcribed audio only: how sure the desk is of the words and the speaker.

fields.name: notes
fields.description: Caveats shown with the quote, for example 'edited clip, time inferred'.

update_log.description: Every check and change, newest first. The newest row that changed something supplies 'The latest' at the top of the page and the page's last-updated time.

fields.name: log_id
fields.description: Permanent id, u plus a number (u001).

fields.name: logged_at
fields.description: When this check or change was made, with the America/New_York offset.

fields.name: run_type
fields.description: What kind of run made the entry.

fields.name: change_type
fields.description: What happened. Use checked_no_change when the run added no source and changed no claim, blocked_source when a source could not be read, and presentation for a change to wording, headings or layout that leaves every finding as it was. checked_no_change and presentation rows never become the latest update.

fields.name: headline
fields.description: One plain sentence a reader could take away, for example 'Investigators recreated the overload in the lab; the root cause is still unclear.' Not 'Morning watch check'.

fields.name: summary
fields.description: What changed and why, in full. Include 'not checked: login required' for blocked sources.

fields.name: claim_ids
fields.description: The claims this entry added or changed, separated by semicolons. Required in practice for added, updated and label_change: the check compares the branch with main and refuses a new row of those types that names no claim the change added or altered (or that a question it answered rests on).

fields.name: author
fields.description: The role that made the entry. Never a person's name. Desk is only for entries made before roles were recorded.
